summary: Behaviour-preserving refactor. InputStreamReader::read() chose how many trailing bytes to withhold at a multibyte boundary by comparing the charset name string ("UTF-8" / "EUC-KR"). That decision now lives in Charset::bytes_to_hold_back, a match over Charset with no wildcard arm, so adding a Charset variant fails to compile until someone decides its boundary rule instead of silently dropping characters.
changes: rustjava-runtime/src/charset.rs: new Charset::bytes_to_hold_back(&[u8]) -> usize; UTF-8 backward scan and EUC-KR forward walk moved verbatim; Iso8859_1 | UsAscii => 0 explicitly
rustjava-runtime/src/classes/java/io/input_stream_reader.rs: read() calls it; name-string branches removed; stale comment at the default ctor reworded
